summary: Vauxhall's typeface is UNIDENTIFIED. No family name, no foundry, no weight set and no ownership status could be evidenced from any reachable source this run. The typography ladder failed at rung 5 (Fonts In Use, WhatTheFont, agency case study) after that rung was actually probed rather than assumed. Rungs 1 to 4 are structurally unreachable. Do NOT accept a plausible-sounding 'Vauxhall Sans': nothing this run supports any family name at all.

ownership.notes: Ownership is answered at the foundry, and no candidate foundry was ever identified, so the question could not be asked. Not probed rather than unpublished.

ladder.rung1_type_spec_or_token_package: unreachable / probed dry by recon. No design system exists and npm plus GitHub were both searched with multiple targeted queries for Vauxhall, Opel and Stellantis. No package.
ladder.rung2_document_fonts_and_fontface_src: NOT PROBED, structurally impossible this run. vauxhall.co.uk is WAF-403, there is no browser and the shell has no internet. This is the rung that would settle it in one call on an unblocked run.
ladder.rung3_font_file_internals: unreachable. No binary can be downloaded to disk this run, so no fontTools inspection was possible. Capability gap, not an absence.
ladder.rung4_brand_guideline_doc: NOT FOUND. Recon established via Wayback that no brand-guideline PDF has ever existed at any guessed path.
ladder.rung5_fontsinuse_whatthefont_case_study: PROBED AND DRY. This is the rung that failed. Detail below.
ladder.rung6_aggregator: NOT PROBED (budget). Brandfetch exposes a claimed typeface field and would be worth one call on a later run, at A4, unverified.

fontsinuse_structured_browse.detail: The Automotive topic holds 331 uses across 5 pages. Page 1 (about 60 entries, sorted by contribution date) contains NO Stellantis-group marque at all: no Vauxhall, Opel, Stellantis, Peugeot, Citroen or General Motors. Marques present instead: Porsche, Maserati, Cadillac, Lincoln, Renault, Aston Martin, Pirelli, Hot Wheels.
fontsinuse_structured_browse.unchecked: pages 2 to 5 of the Automotive topic, and /search/advanced. Budget ran out. Report as unchecked, not absent.

whatthefont.reason: requires uploading a raster sample of the mark. No binary could be downloaded and no screenshot could be captured this run, so there was no sample to submit.

agency_case_study.detail: underconsideration.com Brand New Automobile industry archive page 1 of 9 lists no Vauxhall post. Complete-archive page 1 of 1508 lists no Vauxhall, Opel or Stellantis post. No agency case study for a Vauxhall identity was found. Vauxhall may simply never have been covered.

opel_adjacent.label: ADJACENT EVIDENCE, NOT VAUXHALL EVIDENCE
opel_adjacent.caveat: Opel is Vauxhall's twin brand on a shared platform with a shared CEO (Florian Huettl, 'CEO, Opel and Vauxhall'), and Vauxhall models are re-badged Opels. That makes Opel a useful comparator and NOT proof of anything about Vauxhall's typography. Nothing below may populate a Vauxhall type token.

findings.claim: No Opel corporate typeface was named by any reachable source either.
findings.detail: Opel's own design press category (7 releases, 2013 to 2024) names no typeface and no font family. Neither does the Opel identity post on Brand New, which is paywalled.

related_first_party_design_language_term.note: Not typography, but the only first-party named design vocabulary evidenced this run. Recorded here because a later run may find the typeface documented alongside these terms.

terms.quote: Bold & Pure design language of the Mokka combined with performance accents
including an evolution of the Vauxhall Vizor
terms.note: Confirms 'Vizor' is Vauxhall's own first-party term for its front-end panel, not only Opel's. In this release it is applied to a concept car, not the production model.
Shared with Opel, where it is described as an 'All-digital Pure Panel cockpit' (2021-11-25, media.stellantis.com/em-en/opel/press-category/technology-design).

whatWouldUnblock: One fetch of vauxhall.co.uk with the WAF passed, or any browser session on it, reading @font-face src and document.fonts. That is rung 2 and it would settle family name, weights and the webfont filenames immediately. Failing that, Fonts In Use Automotive pages 2 to 5, or a Brandfetch lookup at A4.
